explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/226 with the Barth–Schneider positive answer. There is an entire F, real on ℝ and not affine on ℝ (so non-linear), such that for real x, x ∈ ℚ iff F(x) ∈ ℚ. Requiring F to be real-valued on ℝ is the natural reading, since rationality of f(x) presupposes a real value. Formal proof linked.
